config.estimand: G = full 336-step cumulative reward; G_r = cumulative reward over all segments of regime r

protocols.within_window: calibrate and test on the same window
protocols.leave_one_window_out: calibrate on the other three windows
protocols.within_regime: calibrate and test on the same regime
protocols.leave_one_regime_out: calibrate on the other four regimes

estimators.identified: h_r + kappa/mu/jump from G0; per-path sigma_open; filter_path belief at each segment start; regime-aware P
estimators.naive: P treated as S; per-path kappa_P/mu_P/sigma_all; no freeze knowledge
estimators.continuous: one model rollout from t=0, conditioned on P_0; regime decomposition of the same rollout
estimators.segment_wise: per-regime segment rollouts re-anchored at the observed position and filtered belief at each segment start

config.paired_comparison: identified vs naive on the same test paths; path-level bootstrap with 2000 resamples, conditioning on the fitted calibration quantiles; full-window uses the continuous rollout, regime-level uses the segment-wise estimator

inputs.note: true S is used in this script only for scoring and truth checks; h and kappa/mu/jump are the G0 estimates, and h was estimated in G0 with true-S diagnostics (not observable-only); per-path sigma and naive parameters use only observable P

filter_vs_kalman_pre_belief.note: filter_path starts from P_0 and filters the full path; kalman_pre_belief starts at the last OPEN before the episode. They should agree at the pre-anchor up to the early-window information.

limits: True S is used only for scoring; in deployment the calibration target (the path's realized reward) requires reconstructing S or an observable-reward variant (D7).

The identified model's h (open_sd/ext_phi/ext_sd/stale_phi/stale_sd) is a G0 estimate obtained with true-S diagnostics, so the pipeline as run is not observable-only; reconstructing h from observables alone is not implemented here (Props 1-2).

The plug-in conditions on the realized future volume path, as steps 5-6 do. Volume is exogenous in the simulator, but future volume is not known at decision time; this is a conditional-on-volume evaluation, not a fully deployable OPE.
Per-path sigma_open/sigma_all and naive kappa_P/mu_P are estimated from the same path's observable P history (transductive), as in step 6; the two estimators use the same information.
kappa/mu/jump and h are fixed G0 estimates shared by calibration and test; they are not re-estimated inside folds.
The regime calendar is deterministic and known at decision time; the model is allowed to know future regime labels.

segment_wise re-anchors at each segment start using the observed position and the filtered belief given P_{0:s}; it is a sum of conditional segment values, not a single continuous rollout. The continuous estimator is the standard model-based rollout.

The regime-level LORO calibration pool contains the other four regime units of each calibration path; units within a path are correlated, so the effective calibration sample is smaller than the nominal 2048 and the pooled quantile has more finite-sample variability than that nominal count suggests. Calibration and test paths are disjoint, so there is no test-path contamination.
Target policies are fixed heuristics, not trained RL policies; the experiment has no IPS/DR or importance weights, only model-based plug-in.

Coverage is marginal over the calibration/test split and pooled over the four held-out groups; per-group numbers are descriptive with binomial SE, not simultaneous. For the regime-level pool the binomial SE over 5x512 units ignores within-path correlation and is systematically understated; inferential claims use the path-level paired bootstrap.
R model draws per path propagate model/MC noise; the 5%/95% quantiles are empirical and therefore noisy at R=32.

The paired identified-vs-naive bootstrap resamples test paths and conditions on the fitted calibration quantiles; it quantifies test-path sampling, not calibration-set uncertainty, and is not simultaneous across scores or regimes.
Per-regime paired differences report a normal-approximation SE; only the pooled paired difference gets a percentile bootstrap CI.
Regime-level pooled coverage averages over the five regime units of each path; per-regime rows are descriptive and not a per-path coverage guarantee.
Identification (Props 5/11) is a population statement; this step is finite-sample coverage, not an identification proof.
